scope: Out-of-period archaeological and local-food validation case for an Inland Niger Delta settlement cluster and its floodplain hinterland.

promotion_audit.decision: Validation-only. The population interval is for a first-millennium urban cluster, not 1337; Jenne-jeno was a trade-connected settlement and its mapped archaeological hinterland is much smaller than the containing EU5 location.

records.label: Jenne-jeno and traditional 1,100 km2 Inland Niger Delta hinterland validation
records.interval_semantics: The 10,000-26,000 interval is a conservative archaeological estimate for Jenne-jeno and satellites within approximately 1 km around AD 800, retained as a historical population validation range. It is not a local Malthusian capacity interval and is not extended to 1337.
pressure_evidence: McIntosh and McIntosh (1981), Journal of African History 22, pp. 1-22, document Jenne-jeno's growth to more than 33 ha by AD 750-1100 and the associated 1,100 km2 traditional hinterland survey.
Archaeological subsistence evidence identifies African rice, fish/fish oil and cattle as the stable Inland Delta food complex supporting permanent floodplain occupation.

The floodplain's annual inundation variability, mound construction above high water and dependence on local rice/fishing/grazing are ecological pressure indicators; the site survey does not establish a saturation fraction.
The region had access to staple products but imported iron, stone and salt; non-local exchange is therefore material for the settlement cluster.
shock_flags: population interval is centered around AD 800, outside 1337
Jenne-jeno is an urban/market cluster and not a rural population label
settlement decline/relocation after AD 1100-1400 is debated
flood regime and malaria/resource shocks are unresolved
iron, stone and salt imports demonstrate trade dependence
source population estimate is archaeological and site-proximate
records.trade_dependence: mixed_to_high for non-food essentials and exchange; staple rice, fish and cattle were locally available but the settlement was a regional trading center
records.boundary_description: The approximately 1,100 km2 Jenne traditional hinterland survey region around Jenne-jeno in the Inland Niger Delta; the 10,000-26,000 population interval itself applies only to the Jenne-jeno/satellite cluster within about 1 km, not all 1,100 km2.
records.boundary_source: McIntosh and McIntosh (1981), site-survey description and Jenne-jeno archaeological sequence
records.boundary_confidence: medium for survey region; low for converting the 1-km settlement cluster into surrounding land capacity
records.source_family_independence: Archaeological population, survey and subsistence evidence are one Jenne-jeno source family; modern environmental summaries are corroborating context only.
citation_details: McIntosh and McIntosh (1981), DOI 10.1017/S0021853700018983: Jenne-jeno apogee 750-1100 and 1,100 km2 traditional hinterland survey.
McIntosh and McIntosh (1979), World Archaeology: African rice, fish and cattle as the stable Inland Delta subsistence complex.
Seshat's synthesis of the archaeological estimate reports 10,000-26,000 for Jenne-jeno and satellites within 1 km around AD 800; treated as validation metadata, not a training target.
records.notes: This case records an African local-floodplain food system with a quantified archaeological population range, but the city/trade and date/boundary constraints explicitly block training use. It may validate whether the mechanistic model can represent African rice/fish/cattle floodplains without applying continental corrections.
